flores_passage_en: Virtually all computers in use today are based on the manipulation of information which is coded in the form of binary numbers. A binary number can have only one of two values, i.e. 0 or 1, and these numbers are referred to as binary digits - or bits, to use computer jargon.
question_en: If computers had been designed to operate using a ternary system (using three values: 0, 1, and 2) instead of a binary system, which of the following consequences would most likely follow based on the passage's description of how modern computers function?
mc_answer1_en: The fundamental nature of information manipulation would remain unchanged, but the system would be slower due to increased complexity in switching between three states.
mc_answer2_en: Computers would require fewer physical components to represent the same amount of information, as each digit could carry more data than a single bit.
mc_answer3_en: Computers would be unable to process any information at all, because the passage states that all current computers rely exclusively on the two-value binary system.
mc_answer4_en: The binary digits would become irrelevant, and computers would need to develop a completely new type of information code that is unrelated to numerical values.
flores_passage: ଆଜିକାଲି ବ୍ୟବହୃତ ହେଉଥିବା ପ୍ରାୟ ସମସ୍ତ କମ୍ପ୍ୟୁଟର ସୂଚନା ପରିଚାଳନା ଉପରେ ଆଧାରିତ ଯାହା ବାଇନାରୀ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଆକାରରେ କୋଡ୍ ହୋଇଛି । ଏକ ବାଇନାରୀ ସଂଖ୍ୟା କେବଳ ଦୁଇଟି ମୂଲ୍ୟ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ ଗୋଟିଏ ହୋଇପାରେ, ଅର୍ଥାତ୍ 0 କିମ୍ବା 1, ଏବଂ ଏହି ସଂଖ୍ୟାଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ ବାଇନାରୀ ଡିଜିଟ୍ - କିମ୍ବା ବିଟ୍ କୁହାଯାଏ, କମ୍ପ୍ୟୁଟର ଜାରଗନ୍ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିବାକୁ ।
question: ଯଦି କମ୍ପ୍ୟୁଟରକୁ ବାଇନାରୀ ସିଷ୍ଟମ ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତେ ଏକ ତ୍ରିଗୁଣୀୟ ସିଷ୍ଟମ (ତିନିଟି ମୂଲ୍ୟଃ ୦, ୧, ଏବଂ ୨) ବ୍ୟବହାର କରି କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ କରିବା ପାଇଁ ଡିଜାଇନ୍ କରାଯାଇଥିଲା, ତେବେ ଆଧୁନିକ କମ୍ପ୍ୟୁଟରଗୁଡିକ କିପରି କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ କରନ୍ତି ତାହା ଉପରେ ଆଧାର କରି ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ପରିଣାମଗୁଡିକ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ କେଉଁଟି ସମ୍ଭବତଃ ଅନୁସରଣ କରିବ?
mc_answer1: ସୂଚନା ପରିଚାଳନା କରିବାର ମୌଳିକ ପ୍ରକୃତି ଅପରିବର୍ତ୍ତିତ ରହିବ, କିନ୍ତୁ ତିନୋଟି ଅବସ୍ଥା ମଧ୍ୟରେ ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତନ କରିବାରେ ଅଧିକ ଜଟିଳତା ହେତୁ ସିଷ୍ଟମ୍ ଧୀର ହେବ ।
mc_answer2: ସମାନ ପରିମାଣର ସୂଚନାକୁ ପ୍ରତିନିଧିତ୍ୱ କରିବା ପାଇଁ କମ୍ପ୍ୟୁଟରଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ କମ୍ ଭୌତିକ ଉପାଦାନ ଆବଶ୍ୟକ ହେବ, ଯେହେତୁ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଅଙ୍କ ଗୋଟିଏ ବିଟ୍ ଅପେକ୍ଷା ଅଧିକ ତଥ୍ୟ ବହନ କରିପାରିବ ।
mc_answer3: କମ୍ପ୍ୟୁଟରଗୁଡ଼ିକ କୌଣସି ସୂଚନା ପ୍ରକ୍ରିୟାକରଣ କରିବାରେ ଅସମର୍ଥ ହେବେ, କାରଣ ଏହି ଅନୁଚ୍ଛେଦରେ କୁହାଯାଇଛି ଯେ ସମସ୍ତ ସାମ୍ପ୍ରତିକ କମ୍ପ୍ୟୁଟରଗୁଡ଼ିକ କେବଳ ଦୁଇ-ମୂଲ୍ୟ ବାଇନାରୀ ସିଷ୍ଟମ ଉପରେ ନିର୍ଭର କରନ୍ତି ।
mc_answer4: ବାଇନାରୀ ଅଙ୍କଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଅପ୍ରାସଙ୍ଗିକ ହୋଇଯିବ, ଏବଂ କମ୍ପ୍ୟୁଟରଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ ଏକ ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ନୂତନ ପ୍ରକାରର ସୂଚନା କୋଡ୍ ବିକଶିତ କରିବାକୁ ପଡିବ ଯାହା ସାଂଖ୍ୟିକ ମୂଲ୍ୟ ସହିତ ଜଡିତ ନୁହେଁ ।

flores_passage_en: One bomb exploded outside the governor general's office. Three more bombs exploded near government buildings in a period of two hours. Some reports put the official death toll at eight, and official reports confirm that up to 30 were injured; but final numbers are not yet known.
question_en: If the initial bomb outside the governor general's office had not exploded, which of the following would most likely have been the immediate consequence based on the passage?
mc_answer1_en: The final number of injured persons would have been exactly 30.
mc_answer2_en: The official death toll would have been zero.
mc_answer3_en: The reports would have confirmed that up to 30 were injured.
mc_answer4_en: Three more bombs might not have exploded near government buildings.

flores_passage_en: During the 18th century Cambodia found itself squeezed between two powerful neighbors, Thailand and Vietnam. The Thais invaded Cambodia several times in the 18th century and in 1772 they destroyed Phnom Phen. In the last years of the 18th century the Vietnamese also invaded Cambodia.
question_en: If the Thais had not destroyed Phnom Penh in 1772, which of the following outcomes would most likely have occurred based on the passage's description of Cambodia's geopolitical situation in the 18th century?
mc_answer1_en: Vietnam would have immediately taken control of Phnom Penh in 1772 regardless of Thai actions.
mc_answer2_en: Cambodia would have avoided all foreign invasions for the remainder of the century.
mc_answer3_en: Cambodia might have maintained a degree of sovereignty for a longer period despite ongoing pressure from both neighbors.
mc_answer4_en: Thailand would have ceased all military activity toward Cambodia after 1772.
flores_passage: ଅଷ୍ଟାଦଶ ଶତାବ୍ଦୀରେ କାମ୍ବୋଡିଆ ଦୁଇ ଶକ୍ତିଶାଳୀ ପଡୋଶୀ ଥାଇଲାଣ୍ଡ ଓ ଭିଏତନାମ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଚାପି ହୋଇ ରହିଥିଲା । ୧୮ଶ ଶତାବ୍ଦୀରେ ଥାଇଲାଣ୍ଡ ଅନେକ ଥର କାମ୍ବୋଡିଆ ଉପରେ ଆକ୍ରମଣ କରିଥିଲା ଏବଂ ୧୭୭୨ରେ ସେମାନେ ଫନମଫେନକୁ ଧ୍ୱଂସ କରିଥିଲେ । ୧୮ଶ ଶତାବ୍ଦୀର ଶେଷ ବର୍ଷରେ ଭିଏତନାମ ମଧ୍ୟ କାମ୍ବୋଡିଆ ଉପରେ ଆକ୍ରମଣ କରିଥିଲା ।
question: ଯଦି ଥାଇଲାଣ୍ଡର ଲୋକମାନେ ୧୭୭୨ ମସିହାରେ ଫନୋମପେନ୍ହକୁ ଧ୍ୱଂସ କରିନଥାନ୍ତେ, ତେବେ ୧୮ଶ ଶତାବ୍ଦୀରେ କାମ୍ବୋଡିଆର ଭୌଗୋଳିକ-ରାଜନୈତିକ ପରିସ୍ଥିତିର ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା ଉପରେ ଆଧାର କରି ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ କେଉଁଟି ସମ୍ଭବତଃ ଘଟିଥାନ୍ତା?
mc_answer1: ଥାଇଲାଣ୍ଡର ପଦକ୍ଷେପକୁ ଖାତିର ନକରି ୧୭୭୨ରେ ଭିଏତନାମ ତୁରନ୍ତ ଫନୋମପେନ୍ହକୁ ନିଜ ନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରଣକୁ ନେଇଥାନ୍ତା ।
mc_answer2: ଶତାବ୍ଦୀର ଅବଶିଷ୍ଟ ସମୟ ପାଇଁ କାମ୍ବୋଡିଆ ସମସ୍ତ ବିଦେଶୀ ଆକ୍ରମଣକୁ ଏଡ଼ାଇ ଦେଇଥାନ୍ତା ।
mc_answer3: ଉଭୟ ପଡୋଶୀଙ୍କ ଚାପ ସତ୍ତ୍ୱେ କାମ୍ବୋଡିଆ ଦୀର୍ଘ ସମୟ ଧରି କିଛି ମାତ୍ରାରେ ସାର୍ବଭୌମତ୍ୱ ବଜାୟ ରଖିପାରିଥାନ୍ତା ।
mc_answer4: ଥାଇଲାଣ୍ଡ ୧୭୭୨ ପରେ କାମ୍ବୋଡିଆ ପ୍ରତି ସମସ୍ତ ସାମରିକ କାର୍ଯ୍ୟକଳାପ ବନ୍ଦ କରିଦେଇଥାନ୍ତା ।

But being placed in the ""high tropics"" just a few degrees north of equator you will need to deal with both heat (always) and strong sun (when the sky is clear, more rarely)."

mc_answer2_en: Visitors would not need to deal with heat as a constant factor.

mc_answer4_en: The availability of goods after arrival would be severely limited.

flores_passage_en: Twentieth century research has shown that there are two pools of genetic variation: hidden and expressed. Mutation adds new genetic variation, and selection removes it from the pool of expressed variation. Segregation and recombination shuffle variation back and forth between the two pools with each generation.
question_en: Based on the passage, what would most likely happen to the pool of expressed genetic variation if mutation ceased to occur while selection continued to remove variation?
mc_answer1_en: The pool of expressed variation would shift entirely into the hidden pool without affecting selection.
mc_answer2_en: The pool of expressed variation would gradually diminish until no new variation was available.
mc_answer3_en: The pool of expressed variation would increase as recombination creates new variants.
mc_answer4_en: The pool of expressed variation would remain constant over time.

flores_passage_en: "Typical for Norway are steep fjords and valleys that suddenly give way to a high, more or less even plateau. These plateaus are often referred to as ""vidde"" meaning a wide, open treeless space, a boundless expanse. In Rogaland and Agder they are usually called ""hei"" meaning a treeless moorland often covered in heather."
question_en: If the steep fjords and valleys of Norway had not suddenly given way to high plateaus, which of the following would most likely be true based on the passage's description of Norwegian geography?
mc_answer1_en: The plateau regions would be replaced by deeper valleys extending indefinitely.
mc_answer2_en: The regions of Rogaland and Agder would likely feature more dense forest coverage.
mc_answer3_en: The landscape would lack the wide, open treeless spaces described as 'vidde' or 'hei'.
mc_answer4_en: The term 'vidde' would no longer exist in Norwegian vocabulary due to lack of physical reference.

flores_passage_en: The fission bomb works on the principle that it takes energy to put together a nucleus with many protons and neutrons. Sort of like rolling a heavy cart up a hill. Splitting the nucleus up again then releases some of that energy. Some atoms have unstable nuclei which means that they tend to break apart with little or no nudging.
question_en: If the principle of nuclear fission relied on energy being released to assemble a nucleus rather than split it, what would be the likely outcome for an unstable atom that naturally breaks apart with little nudging?
mc_answer1_en: The atom would spontaneously release energy upon assembling a nucleus, making it unstable.
mc_answer2_en: The atom would require an external energy input to prevent it from breaking apart.

question_en: If Nigeria had not announced its intention to join the AfCFTA in the week leading up to the summit, what would most likely have been the consequence based on the passage's context regarding the framework's readiness?

mc_answer3_en: The rules of origin and tariff concessions would have been immediately agreed upon.
mc_answer4_en: The framework would not have been sufficient to start trading on July 1, 2020.

flores_passage_en: Romanticism had a large element of cultural determinism, drawn from writers such as Goethe, Fichte, and Schlegel. In the context of Romanticism, the geography molded individuals, and over time customs and culture related to that geography arose, and these, being in harmony with the place of the society, were better than arbitrarily imposed laws.
question_en: According to the passage, what would most likely have been the result if Romanticism had not embraced cultural determinism from writers like Goethe, Fichte, and Schlegel?
mc_answer1_en: Customs and culture would have arisen independently of geographical influences and become superior to place-based harmony.
mc_answer2_en: Society would have developed arbitrary laws that conflicted with local customs and geography.
mc_answer3_en: Romanticism would have focused solely on individualism rather than collective cultural development.
mc_answer4_en: Geography would have ceased to influence individual development and cultural evolution.

flores_passage_en: The South Pole Traverse (or Highway) is a 1600 km trail from McMurdo Station on the Ross Sea to the Pole. It's compacted snow with crevasses filled in and marked by flags. It can only be traveled by specialized tractors, hauling sleds with fuel and supplies. These aren't very nimble so the trail has to take a long swerve around the Transantarctic Mountains to come onto the plateau.
question_en: If the specialized tractors used on the South Pole Traverse were significantly more nimble, how would the route to the Pole likely change based on the passage's description of current travel constraints?
mc_answer1_en: The trail would need to become even longer to ensure fuel sleds could navigate steeper terrain safely.
mc_answer2_en: The trail could take a more direct path, potentially avoiding the long swerve around the Transantarctic Mountains.
mc_answer3_en: The trail would require specialized tractors to be replaced with aircraft to maintain the compacted snow surface.
mc_answer4_en: The trail would remain unchanged because crevasses still need to be filled in regardless of vehicle type.

flores_passage_en: Pre-modern observatories are usually obsolete today, and remain as museums, or sites of education. As light pollution in their heyday was not the kind of problem it is today, they are usually located in cities or at campuses, easier to reach than those built in modern times. Most modern research telescopes are enormous facilities in remote areas with favorable atmospheric conditions.
question_en: If light pollution had not been a significant issue in the heyday of pre-modern observatories, how would their locations likely have been different according to the passage?

mc_answer2_en: They would have been constructed as enormous facilities like modern research telescopes.
mc_answer3_en: They would have been built in remote areas to avoid atmospheric interference.
mc_answer4_en: They would have been designed primarily for educational purposes rather than observation.

flores_passage_en: "Around the 15th century, northern Estonia was under great cultural influence of Germany. Some German monks wanted to bring God closer to the native people, so they invented the Estonian literal language. It was based on the German alphabet and one character ""Õ/õ"" was added. As time passed, many words that were borrowed from German coalesced. This was the beginning of enlightenment."
question_en: Based on the passage, what would most likely have happened to the Estonian written language if the German monks had not decided to bring God closer to the native people?
mc_answer1_en: It might have remained purely oral with no standardized written form based on the German alphabet.
mc_answer2_en: The German alphabet would have been used unchanged without the addition of the character 'Õ/õ' even after enlightenment.
mc_answer3_en: It would have immediately adopted the Latin alphabet and fully integrated French vocabulary.
mc_answer4_en: The native people would have created their own alphabet using runes without any German influence.

flores_passage_en: Vatican City's population is around 800. It is the smallest independent country in the world and the country with the lowest population. Vatican City uses Italian in its legislation and official communications. Italian is also the everyday language used by most of those who work in the state while Latin is often used in religious ceremonies. All citizens of Vatican City are Roman Catholic.
question_en: If Latin were no longer used in religious ceremonies in Vatican City, which of the following outcomes would most likely occur based on the passage's description of language usage?
mc_answer1_en: The population of Vatican City would decrease significantly.
mc_answer2_en: Italian would likely replace Latin as the primary language for religious ceremonies.
mc_answer3_en: The country would cease to use Italian in its legislation.
mc_answer4_en: Vatican City would no longer be the smallest independent country in the world.

flores_passage_en: "Parisians have a reputation for being egocentric, rude and arrogant. While this is often only an inaccurate stereotype, the best way to get along in Paris still is to be on your best behavior, acting like someone who is ""bien élevé"" (well brought up). It will make getting about considerably easier. Parisians' abrupt exteriors will rapidly evaporate if you display some basic courtesies."
question_en: What would likely happen if a tourist in Paris behaved without basic courtesies, contrary to the advice given in the passage?
mc_answer1_en: Their interactions with Parisians would likely remain difficult despite their good intentions.
mc_answer2_en: Parisians' abrupt exteriors would vanish immediately regardless of the tourist's behavior.

flores_passage_en: Golf is a game in which players use clubs to hit balls into holes. Eighteen holes are played during a regular round, with players usually starting on the first hole on the course and finishing on the eighteenth. The player who takes the fewest strokes, or swings of the club, to complete the course wins. The game is played on grass, and the grass around the hole is mown shorter and called the green.
question_en: If the grass around the hole had not been mown shorter, what would most likely have happened to the game's outcome?
mc_answer1_en: Players would have used fewer clubs to hit the ball into the holes.
mc_answer2_en: The game would have ended after only eight holes instead of eighteen.
mc_answer3_en: The ball would have rolled more slowly, potentially increasing the number of strokes required to reach the hole.
mc_answer4_en: The player who starts on the first hole would have won regardless of stroke count.

flores_passage_en: "There are many things you have to take into consideration before and when you travel somewhere. When you travel, expect things not to be like they are ""back home"". Manners, laws, food, traffic, lodging, standards, language and so on will to some extent differ from where you live. This is something you always need to keep in mind, to avoid disappointment or perhaps even distaste over local ways to do things."
question_en: According to the passage, if a traveler had not taken local customs, laws, and standards into consideration before their trip, what would most likely be the outcome?
mc_answer1_en: They would automatically adapt to the new environment without any issues.
mc_answer2_en: They would experience disappointment or distaste over local ways of doing things.
mc_answer3_en: They would be able to ignore the differences without consequence.
mc_answer4_en: They would find the local customs to be exactly the same as back home.

flores_passage_en: Everyone participates in society and uses transportation systems. Almost everyone complains about transportation systems. In developed countries you seldom hear similar levels of complaints about water quality or bridges falling down. Why do transportation systems engender such complaints, why do they fail on a daily basis? Are transportation engineers just incompetent? Or is something more fundamental going on?
question_en: If transportation systems had not been designed to accommodate the high volume of daily users, what would most likely be the consequence based on the passage's reasoning about complaints and failures?
mc_answer1_en: Complaints about transportation would remain high because the issue is fundamental, not just design volume.
mc_answer2_en: Transportation systems would fail less frequently, reducing daily complaints.
mc_answer3_en: Complaints about water quality and bridges would increase to match transportation complaints.
mc_answer4_en: Transportation engineers would become more competent, solving the issue.

The problem is that snow is sticky, so it needs some triggering to come down, and some snow coming down can be the triggering event for the rest. question_en: According to the passage, what would most likely happen if human activity were not a triggering event for avalanches on steep slopes?

mc_answer4_en: Snow would become less sticky and require no triggering at all.

flores_passage_en: The cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro had a flush toilet in almost every house, attached to a sophisticated sewage system. Its remnants produced showers across most of the islands, though as of yet, no damage or flooding has been reported. flores_passage_en: Rules regarding regular photography also apply to video recording, possibly even more so. If just taking a photo of something isn't allowed, then you shouldn't even think of recording a video of it. If using a drone, check well in advance as to what you are allowed to film and what permits or additional licensing are required. Flying a drone near an airport or over a crowd is almost always a bad idea, even if it's not illegal in your area.
question_en: According to the passage, what would be the most appropriate action if someone had not checked the specific filming regulations and permits required before using a drone?
mc_answer1_en: They should cancel or delay the drone filming until they have verified the allowed areas and necessary permits.
mc_answer2_en: They should record a video anyway, since video recording rules are less strict than photography rules.
mc_answer3_en: They should fly the drone near an airport to test the regulations, as this is a good practice for understanding local laws.
mc_answer4_en: They should proceed with filming, assuming that general rules for photography would suffice.

flores_passage_en: The Twin Otter had been trying to land at Kokoda yesterday as Airlines PNG Flight CG4684, but had aborted once already. About ten minutes before it was due to land from its second approach it disapeared. The crash site was located today and is so inaccessable that two policemen were dropped into the jungle in order to hike to the scene and seek survivors. The search had been hampered by the same bad weather that had caused the aborted landing.
question_en: If the weather had not been bad, what would most likely have been the outcome of the Twin Otter's second approach?
mc_answer1_en: The plane would have landed but the search team would still have been sent to investigate a minor incident.
mc_answer2_en: The plane would have landed successfully and no search for survivors would have been necessary.
mc_answer3_en: The plane would have aborted the landing a third time regardless of weather conditions.
mc_answer4_en: The plane would have crashed anyway because the pilot was inexperienced.

flores_passage_en: Phnom Krom, 12 km southwest of Siem Reap. This hilltop temple was built at the end of the 9th century, during the reign of King Yasovarman. The gloomy atmosphere of the temple and the view over the Tonle Sap lake make the climb to the hill worthwhile. A visit to the site can be conveniently combined with a boat trip to the lake. The Angkor Pass is needed to enter the temple so do not forget to bring your passport along when heading to Tonle Sap.
question_en: If King Yasovarman had not built the Phnom Krom temple at the end of the 9th century, which of the following outcomes would most likely have occurred according to the passage's implied context?
mc_answer1_en: The climb to the hill would still be considered worthwhile due to the lake view.
mc_answer2_en: Visitors would not need to bring their passport for the temple entry.

flores_passage_en: Unlike other primates, hominids no longer use their hands in locomotion or bearing weight or swinging through the trees. The chimpanzee's hand and foot are similar in size and length, reflecting the hand's use for bearing weight in knuckle walking. The human hand is shorter than the foot, with straighter phalanges. Fossil hand bones two million to three million years old reveal this shift in specialization of the hand from locomotion to manipulation.
question_en: According to the passage, if hominids had continued to use their hands in locomotion and bearing weight as chimpanzees do, which of the following structural characteristics of the human hand would most likely still be present?

mc_answer3_en: The human hand would have evolved to be longer than the foot.
mc_answer4_en: The human hand would have developed knuckle-walking adaptations similar to modern apes.

flores_passage_en: Elements and compounds can move from one state to another and not change. Nitrogen as a gas still has the same properties as liquid nitrogen. The liquid state is denser but the molecules are still the same. Water is another example. The compound water is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. It has the same molecular structure whether it is a gas, liquid, or solid. Although its physical state may change, its chemical state remains the same.
question_en: According to the passage, what would likely happen to the chemical properties of nitrogen if it were to transition from a liquid state back to a gaseous state, assuming no external chemical reactions occurred?
mc_answer1_en: The chemical properties would become identical to those of water vapor due to shared atomic composition.
mc_answer2_en: The chemical properties would remain the same as they are in the liquid state.
mc_answer3_en: The chemical properties would change because the molecules would rearrange into a different compound.
mc_answer4_en: The chemical properties would become less dense and lose their molecular structure.

flores_passage_en: Things did not go well for the Italians in North Africa almost from the start. Within a week of Italy's declaration of war on June 10, 1940, the British 11th Hussars had seized Fort Capuzzo in Libya. In an ambush east of Bardia, the British captured the Italian Tenth Army's Engineer-in-Chief, General Lastucci. On June 28, Marshal Italo Balbo, the Governor-General of Libya and apparent heir to Mussolini, was killed by friendly fire while landing in Tobruk.
question_en: If Marshal Italo Balbo had not been killed by friendly fire while landing in Tobruk on June 28, 1940, which of the following outcomes is most likely based on the passage's description of the Italian situation in North Africa?
mc_answer1_en: General Lastucci would have been promoted to Marshal immediately after the ambush at Bardia.
mc_answer2_en: The Italian Tenth Army's morale and leadership structure might have been preserved, potentially altering early campaign dynamics.
mc_answer3_en: The British would have declared war on Italy a week earlier than June 10, 1940.
mc_answer4_en: The British 11th Hussars would have immediately surrendered Fort Capuzzo.

flores_passage_en: Travelling by plane can be a scary experience for people of all ages and backgrounds, particularly if they've not flown before or have experienced a traumatic event. It is not something to be ashamed of: it is no different from the personal fears and dislikes of other things that very many people have. For some, understanding something about how aircraft work and what happens during a flight may help to overcome a fear which is based on the unknown or on not being in control.
question_en: According to the passage, if a passenger had not experienced a traumatic event in the past, which of the following would most likely be true about their fear of flying?
mc_answer1_en: They would definitely not experience any fear of flying at all.
mc_answer2_en: They would only fear flying if they had not understood how aircraft work.
mc_answer3_en: They would fear flying more than someone who had experienced a traumatic event.
mc_answer4_en: They would still potentially experience fear, as flying can be scary regardless of prior trauma.

flores_passage_en: Gothic style peaked in the period between the 10th - 11th centuries and the 14th century. At the beginning dress was heavily influenced by the Byzantine culture in the east. However, due to the slow communication channels, styles in the west could lag behind by 25 to 30 year. towards the end of the Middle Ages western Europe began to develop their own style. one of the biggest developments of the time as a result of the crusades people began to use buttons to fasten clothing.
question_en: If the communication channels between the east and west had been faster during the Gothic period, which of the following outcomes would most likely have occurred according to the passage?
mc_answer1_en: The Gothic style would have peaked earlier than the 10th century due to accelerated cultural exchange.
mc_answer2_en: Western Europe would have adopted Byzantine dress styles more quickly, reducing the lag time between cultural influences.
mc_answer3_en: Western Europe would have developed their own style independently without any Byzantine influence.
mc_answer4_en: The use of buttons in clothing would have been introduced earlier due to increased trade with the east.

flores_passage_en: Red tide is caused by a higher than normal concentration of Karenia brevis, a naturally-occurring single-celled marine organism. Natural factors can intersect to produce ideal conditions, allowing this algae to increase in number dramatically. The algae produces a neurotoxin that can disable nerves in both humans and fish. Fish often die because of the high concentrations of the toxin in the waters. Humans can be affected by breathing affected water taken into the air by wind and waves.
question_en: If natural factors had not intersected to produce ideal conditions for Karenia brevis, which of the following would most likely have occurred regarding human health impacts from red tide?
mc_answer1_en: Humans would have been unaffected by red tide neurotoxins because the algae would not have increased in number dramatically.
mc_answer2_en: Fish would have died despite the absence of ideal conditions due to natural concentrations of Karenia brevis.
mc_answer3_en: Wind and waves would have dispersed neurotoxins more effectively, reducing human exposure even without ideal conditions.
mc_answer4_en: The neurotoxin would have remained harmless to both fish and humans regardless of algae concentration.
flores_passage: ରେଡ ଟାଇଡ (Red tide) ର କାରଣ ହେଉଛି କରେନିଆ ବ୍ରେଭିସ (Karenia brevis) ର ସ୍ୱାଭାବିକ ଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ଏକାଗ୍ରତା, ଏକ ପ୍ରାକୃତିକ ଭାବରେ ଦେଖାଯାଉଥିବା ଏକକ-କୋଷୀୟ ସାମୁଦ୍ରିକ ଜୀବ । ପ୍ରାକୃତିକ କାରକଗୁଡିକ ଆଦର୍ଶ ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ସୃଷ୍ଟି କରିବା ପାଇଁ ପରସ୍ପରକୁ କଣ୍ଟାକ୍ଟ କରିପାରନ୍ତି, ଯାହା ଏହି ଆଲ୍ଗେକୁ ନାଟକୀୟ ଭାବରେ ବୃଦ୍ଧି କରିବାକୁ ଅନୁମତି ଦେଇଥାଏ । ଆଲ୍ଗେ ଏକ ନ୍ୟୁରୋଟକ୍ସିନ ଉତ୍ପାଦନ କରେ ଯାହା ଉଭୟ ମଣିଷ ଏବଂ ମାଛଙ୍କ ସ୍ nervous ାଙ୍ଗକୁ ଅକ୍ଷମ କରିପାରେ । ଜଳରେ ଟକ୍ସିନର ଉଚ୍ଚ ଏକାଗ୍ରତା ହେତୁ ମାଛମାନେ ଅନେକ ସମୟରେ ମୃତ୍ୟୁବରଣ କରନ୍ତି । ପବନ ଏବଂ ତରଙ୍ଗ ଦ୍ୱାରା ବାୟୁରେ ନିଆଯାଇଥିବା ପ୍ରଭାବିତ ଜଳ ଶ୍ୱାସକ୍ରିୟା ଦ୍ୱାରା ମଣିଷ ପ୍ରଭାବିତ ହୋଇପାରେ ।

flores_passage_en: The Babylonians built each of their gods a primary temple that was considered the home of the god. People would bring sacrifices to the gods and the priests would try to attend to the needs of the gods through ceremonies and festivals. Each temple had an open temple courtyard and then an inner sanctuary that only the priests could enter. Sometimes special pyramid shaped towers, called ziggurats, were built to be a part of the temples. The top of the tower was special sanctuary for the god.
question_en: If the priests had not been allowed to enter the inner sanctuary of the temple, what would most likely have been the consequence?
mc_answer1_en: The ziggurats would have been built as open-air courtyards instead.
mc_answer2_en: The ceremonies and festivals would have been disrupted or incomplete.
mc_answer3_en: The gods would have received no sacrifices from the people.
mc_answer4_en: The primary temple would have been converted into a public marketplace.

question: ଯଦି ଗଭର୍ଣ୍ଣର ପେରୀ ନାଗରିକମାନଙ୍କୁ ଆଶ୍ୱାସନା ଦେଇନଥାନ୍ତେ ଯେ 'ସାର୍ବଜନୀନ ନିରାପତ୍ତା ରକ୍ଷା ପାଇଁ ପଦକ୍ଷେପ ନିଆଯାଉଛି,' ତେବେ ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ପରିଣାମ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ କେଉଁଟି ଅନୁମାନ କରାଯାଇପାରେ?

flores_passage_en: One of the most common problems when trying to convert a movie to DVD format is the overscan. Most televisions are made in a way to please the general public. For that reason, everything you see on the TV had the borders cut, top, bottom and sides. This is made to ensure that the image covers the whole screen. That is called overscan. Unfortunately, when you make a DVD, it's borders will most likely be cut too, and if the video had subtitles too close to the bottom, they won't be fully shown.
question_en: If the television manufacturers had not implemented overscan to ensure the image covers the whole screen, what would most likely be the consequence for DVD subtitles?
mc_answer1_en: Subtitles would appear cut off at the bottom of the screen
mc_answer2_en: DVD borders would be automatically adjusted to fit the screen
mc_answer3_en: The video would be displayed in a smaller area than the screen
mc_answer4_en: Subtitles would remain fully visible without being cut

flores_passage_en: "Since Montevideo is south of the Equator, it is summer there when it's winter in the Northern Hemisphere and vice versa. Montevideo is in the subtropics; in the summer months, temperatures above +30°C are common. The winter can be deceptively chilly: temperatures rarely go below freezing, but the wind and humidity combine to make it feel colder than what the thermometer says. There are no particular ""rainy"" and ""dry"" seasons: the amount of rain stays roughly the same throughout the year."
question_en: If Montevideo had been located in the Northern Hemisphere instead of the Southern Hemisphere, which of the following would most likely be true regarding its seasonal climate patterns compared to its actual conditions?
mc_answer1_en: It would never experience temperatures above +30°C during any season.
mc_answer2_en: It would have distinct rainy and dry seasons, unlike the current climate.
mc_answer3_en: It would experience winter conditions that feel colder than the thermometer indicates due to wind and humidity.
mc_answer4_en: Temperatures above +30°C would still be common during what is currently considered its summer months.

flores_passage_en: This is believed to be the fifth time in history that people have observed what turned out to be chemically confirmed martian material falling to Earth. Out of the approximately 24,000 known meteorites to have fallen to Earth, only about 34 have been verified to be martian in origin. Some of the rocks, which are very rare on Earth, are being sold from US$11,000 to $22,500 per ounce, which is about ten times more than the cost of gold.
question_en: Based on the passage, what would most likely have been the consequence if the meteorite shower last July had not occurred?
mc_answer1_en: The total number of meteorites falling to Earth would have decreased by 24,000.
mc_answer2_en: People would have stopped buying meteorites for scientific research.
mc_answer3_en: The price of martian meteorites would have dropped significantly below the cost of gold.
mc_answer4_en: The number of known meteorites from Mars would have remained at approximately 19 rather than increasing to 34.

flores_passage_en: "The ""up bow"" mark looks like a V and the ""down bow mark"" like a staple or a square missing its bottom side. Up means you should start at the tip and push the bow, and down means you should start at the frog (which is where your hand is holding the bow) and pull the bow. An up-bow usually generates a softer sound, while a down-bow is stronger and more assertive. Feel free to pencil in your own marks, but remember the printed bowing marks are there for a musical reason, so they should usually be respected."

mc_answer1_en: The music would sound softer and less assertive at those moments.

flores_passage_en: For some festivals, the vast majority of the attendants to music festivals decide to camp on site, and most attendants consider it a vital part of the experience. If you want to be close to the action you're going to have to get in early to get a camping site close to the music. Remember that even though music on the main stages may have finished, there may be sections of the festival that will keep playing music until late into the night. Some festivals have special camping areas for families with young children.
question_en: Based on the passage, what would most likely happen if a festival attendee wanted to camp close to the main stages but arrived after the camping sites had already been claimed by early arrivals?
mc_answer1_en: They would be unable to secure a spot near the main stages and might need to camp further away.
mc_answer2_en: They would be guaranteed a spot near the main stages because festivals prioritize early arrivals.
mc_answer3_en: They would automatically be moved to a special family camping area regardless of their preference.
mc_answer4_en: They would be allowed to camp near the main stages if they waited until late at night.

flores_passage_en: Time is something that is all around us, and affects everything we do, yet is difficult to understand. Time has been studied by religious, philosophical, and scientific scholars for thousands of years. We experience time as a series of events passing from the future through the present to the past. Time is also how we compare the duration (length) of events. You can mark the passing of time yourself by observing the repetition of a cyclical event. A cyclical event is something that happens again and again regularly.
question_en: If the concept of cyclical events did not exist, what would be the most likely consequence for how humans experience time according to the passage?
mc_answer1_en: The future would become indistinguishable from the past
mc_answer2_en: Time would cease to be studied by scholars
mc_answer3_en: Humans would be unable to mark the passing of time themselves
mc_answer4_en: Events would no longer have a duration or length

flores_passage_en: The Plitvice Lakes national park is heavily forested, mainly with beech, spruce, and fir trees, and features a mixture of Alpine and Mediterranean vegetation. It has a notably wide variety of plant communities, due to its range of microclimates, differing soils and varying levels of altitude. The area is also home to an extremely wide variety of animal and bird species. Rare fauna such as the European brown bear, wolf, eagle, owl, lynx, wild cat and capercaillie can be found there, along with many more common species
question_en: If the Plitvice Lakes national park had not been heavily forested with beech, spruce, and fir trees, which of the following would most likely have been impacted according to the passage?
mc_answer1_en: The area would have supported fewer rare animal species due to reduced habitat diversity.
mc_answer2_en: The park would have lacked the mixture of Alpine and Mediterranean vegetation described.
mc_answer3_en: The altitude levels across the park would have been altered to favor only Mediterranean species.
mc_answer4_en: The range of microclimates and varying soil levels would have changed significantly.

flores_passage_en: Cinque Terre, which means Five Lands, comprises the five small coastal villages of Riomaggiore, Manarola, Corniglia, Vernazza and Monterosso located in the Italian region of Liguria. They are listed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Over the centuries, people have carefully built terraces on the rugged, steep landscape right up to the cliffs that overlook the sea. Part of its charm is the lack of visible corporate development. Paths, trains and boats connect the villages, and cars cannot reach them from the outside.
question_en: If the terraces built by people over the centuries had not been constructed on the rugged, steep landscape, which of the following outcomes would most likely have occurred?
mc_answer1_en: The villages would have been accessible by cars from the outside.
mc_answer2_en: The paths, trains, and boats would have been replaced by a different transportation system.
mc_answer3_en: The villages would have lacked the distinctive charm that comes from their unique terraced landscape.
mc_answer4_en: The villages would have been removed from the UNESCO World Heritage List.

flores_passage_en: Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth, and surrounds the South Pole. Tourist visits are costly, demand physical fitness, can only take place in summer Nov-Feb, and are largely limited to the Peninsula, Islands and Ross Sea. A couple of thousand staff live here in summer in some four dozen bases mostly in those areas; a small number stay over winter. Inland Antarctica is a desolate plateau covered by 2-3 km of ice. Occasional specialist air tours go inland, for mountaineering or to reach the Pole, which has a large base.
question_en: If the summer season (Nov-Feb) were unavailable for tourist visits to Antarctica, which of the following would most likely be true based on the passage?
mc_answer1_en: The large base at the Pole would become inaccessible to all visitors.
mc_answer2_en: Tourist visits would be limited to specialist air tours only.
mc_answer3_en: Staff living in the bases would no longer be needed during the year.
mc_answer4_en: Inland Antarctica would see a surge in mountaineering expeditions.

flores_passage_en: If you want to see the world on the cheap, for necessity, lifestyle or challenge, there are some ways to do that. Basically, they fall into two categories: Either work while you travel or try and limit your expenses. This article is focused on the latter. For those willing to sacrifice comfort, time and predictability to push expenses down close to zero, see minimum budget travel. The advice assumes that travellers do not steal, trespass, participate in the illegal market, beg, or otherwise exploit other people for their own gain.
question_en: According to the passage, what would most likely happen if a traveler decided to engage in begging to reduce expenses?
mc_answer1_en: The traveler would violate the article's core ethical assumptions.
mc_answer2_en: The traveler would be exempt from sacrificing comfort and time.
mc_answer3_en: The traveler would successfully achieve minimum budget travel.
mc_answer4_en: The traveler would be encouraged to participate in the illegal market.
flores_passage: ଯଦି ଆପଣ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା, ଜୀବନଶୈଳୀ କିମ୍ବା ଆହ୍ୱାନ ପାଇଁ ଶସ୍ତାରେ ଦୁନିଆ ଦେଖିବାକୁ ଚାହାଁନ୍ତି, ତେବେ ଏଥିପାଇଁ କିଛି ଉପାୟ ଅଛି । ମୂଳତଃ, ସେଗୁଡିକ ଦୁଇଟି ଶ୍ରେଣୀରେ ବଣ୍ଟା ଯାଇଥାଏ: ଆପଣ ଯାତ୍ରା କରିବା ସମୟରେ କାମ କରନ୍ତୁ କିମ୍ବା ଆପଣଙ୍କର ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚକୁ ସୀମିତ କରିବାକୁ ଚେଷ୍ଟା କରନ୍ତୁ । ଏହି ଆର୍ଟିକିଲ୍ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଉପରେ ଧ୍ୟାନ ଦେଇଥାଏ । ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚକୁ ଶୂନ ନିକଟକୁ ଆଣିବା ପାଇଁ ଆରାମ, ସମୟ ଏବଂ ପୂର୍ବାନୁମାନକୁ ବଳିଦାନ ଦେବାକୁ ଇଚ୍ଛୁକ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ, ସର୍ବନିମ୍ନ ବଜେଟ୍ ଭ୍ରମଣ ଦେଖନ୍ତୁ । ପରାମର୍ଶ ଏହା ଧାରଣ କରେ ଯେ ଭ୍ରମଣକାରୀମାନେ ଚୋରି କରନ୍ତି ନାହିଁ, ବେଆଇନ ବଜାରରେ ଅଂଶଗ୍ରହଣ କରନ୍ତି ନାହିଁ, ଭିକ ମାଗନ୍ତି ନାହିଁ କିମ୍ବା ଅନ୍ୟ ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ନିଜ ଲାଭ ପାଇଁ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରନ୍ତି ନାହିଁ ।

flores_passage_en: German pastries are quite good, and in Bavaria, are quite rich and varied, similar to those of their southern neighbor, Austria. Fruit pastries are common, with apples cooked into pastries year round, and cherries and plums making their appearances during the summer. Many German baked goods also feature almonds, hazelnuts, and other tree nuts. Popular cakes often pair particularly well with a cup of strong coffee. If you want some small though rich pastries, try what depending on region are called Berliner, Pfannkuchen or Krapfen.
question_en: According to the passage, if cherries and plums were not available during the summer, which of the following would most likely occur?
mc_answer1_en: Almonds and hazelnuts would replace cherries and plums as the main fruit fillings.
mc_answer2_en: Apples would likely remain the primary fruit used in pastries throughout the year.
mc_answer3_en: Strong coffee would no longer pair well with popular cakes.
mc_answer4_en: The variety of German pastries in Bavaria would decrease to match Austrian standards.

flores_passage_en: Travel agencies have been around since the 19th century. A travel agent is usually a good option for a journey which extends beyond a traveller's previous experience of nature, culture, language or low-income countries. Although most agencies are willing to take on most regular bookings, many agents specialise in particular types of travel, budget ranges or destinations. It can be better to use an agent who frequently books similar trips to yours. Take a look at what trips the agent is promoting, whether on a website or in a shop window.
question_en: If a travel agency had not existed in the 19th century, what would be the most likely consequence for travelers seeking experiences in low-income countries or unfamiliar cultural environments?
mc_answer1_en: The demand for travel would have decreased significantly due to increased costs.
mc_answer2_en: All travelers would have avoided international destinations altogether.
mc_answer3_en: Travel agencies would have developed entirely different business models focused only on luxury destinations.
mc_answer4_en: Travelers would have had to rely solely on personal networks and word-of-mouth for trip planning and cultural guidance.
flores_passage: ଭ୍ରମଣ ଏଜେନ୍ସିଗୁଡିକ ୧୯ ଶତାବ୍ଦୀରୁ ରହିଆସିଛି । ଏକ ଭ୍ରମଣ ଏଜେନ୍ସି ସାଧାରଣତଃ ଏକ ଯାତ୍ରା ପାଇଁ ଏକ ଭଲ ବିକଳ୍ପ ଅଟେ ଯାହା ପ୍ରକୃତି, ସଂସ୍କୃତି, ଭାଷା କିମ୍ବା ନିମ୍ନ ଆୟକାରୀ ଦେଶଗୁଡିକର ଜଣେ ଭ୍ରମଣକାରୀଙ୍କ ପୂର୍ବ ଅଭିଜ୍ଞତା ବାହାରେ ବ୍ୟାପିଥାଏ । ଯଦିଓ ଅଧିକାଂଶ ଏଜେନ୍ସି ଅଧିକାଂଶ ନିୟମିତ ବୁକିଂ ନେବାକୁ ଇଚ୍ଛୁକ, ଅନେକ ଏଜେଣ୍ଟ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ପ୍ରକାରର ଭ୍ରମଣ, ବଜେଟ୍ ରେଞ୍ଜ କିମ୍ବା ଗନ୍ତବ୍ୟ ସ୍ଥଳରେ ବିଶେଷଜ୍ଞ ଅଟନ୍ତି । ଏକ ଏଜେଣ୍ଟ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିବା ଭଲ ହୋଇପାରେ ଯିଏ ବାରମ୍ବାର ଆପଣଙ୍କ ପରି ଭ୍ରମଣ ବୁକ୍ କରେ । ଏଜେଣ୍ଟ କେଉଁ ଭ୍ରମଣକୁ ପ୍ରୋତ୍ସାହିତ କରୁଛି ତାହା ଏକ ୱେବସାଇଟ୍ କିମ୍ବା ଏକ ଦୋକାନ ୱିଣ୍ଡୋରେ ଦେଖନ୍ତୁ ।
question: ଯଦି ଉନବିଂଶ ଶତାବ୍ଦୀରେ କୌଣସି ଟ୍ରାଭେଲ ଏଜେନ୍ସି ନ ଥାନ୍ତା, ତେବେ ନିମ୍ନ ଆୟକାରୀ ଦେଶ କିମ୍ବା ଅଜଣା ସାଂସ୍କୃତିକ ପରିବେଶରେ ଅନୁଭୂତି ଖୋଜୁଥିବା ଯାତ୍ରୀମାନଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ କ'ଣ ସବୁଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପରିଣାମ ହୋଇଥାନ୍ତା?

mc_answer3: ଭ୍ରମଣ ଏଜେନ୍ସିଗୁଡ଼ିକ ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଭିନ୍ନ ବ୍ୟବସାୟ ମଡେଲ ବିକଶିତ କରିଥାଆନ୍ତେ ଯାହା କେବଳ ବିଳାସପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଗନ୍ତବ୍ୟସ୍ଥଳ ଉପରେ କେନ୍ଦ୍ରିତ ହୋଇଥାଆନ୍ତା ।

flores_passage_en: The capital of Moldova is Chişinău. The local language is Romanian, but Russian is widely used. Moldova is a multi-ethnic republic that has suffered from ethnic conflict. In 1994, this conflict led to the creation of the self-proclaimed Transnistria Republic in eastern Moldova, which has its own government and currency but is not recognised by any UN member country. Economic links have been re-established between these two parts of Moldova despite the failure in political negotiations. The major religion in Moldova is Orthodox Christian.
question_en: If the 1994 ethnic conflict had not occurred in Moldova, which of the following outcomes would most likely be true based on the passage?
mc_answer1_en: Economic links between the two parts of Moldova would have been completely severed.
mc_answer2_en: Moldova would not have a self-proclaimed republic with its own government and currency in the east.
mc_answer3_en: Transnistria would have been recognized as a UN member country.
mc_answer4_en: The local language in Moldova would have changed to Russian exclusively.

flores_passage_en: For those unfamiliar with medical jargon, the words infectious and contagious have distinct meanings. An infectious disease is one that is caused by a pathogen, such as a virus, bacterium, fungus or other parasites. A contagious disease is a disease which is easily transmitted by being in the vicinity of an infected person. Many governments require visitors entering, or residents leaving, their countries to be vaccinated for a range of diseases. These requirements may often depend on what countries a traveller has visited or intends to visit.
question_en: If a government had not required vaccination for visitors entering their country, what would most likely have occurred based on the passage's definition of infectious diseases?
mc_answer1_en: The distinction between infectious and contagious diseases would have become irrelevant.
mc_answer2_en: Governments would have stopped tracking which countries travelers visited.
mc_answer3_en: Travelers with infectious diseases could have entered the country without restriction, potentially spreading pathogens like viruses or bacteria.
mc_answer4_en: All contagious diseases would have automatically been eliminated from the population.

flores_passage_en: The games kicked off at 10:00am with great weather and apart from mid morning drizzle which quickly cleared up, it was a perfect day for 7's rugby. Tournament top seeds South Africa started on the right note when they had a comfortable 26 - 00 win against 5th seeded Zambia. Looking decidedly rusty in the game against their southern sisters, South Africa however steadily improved as the tournament progressed. Their disciplined defence, ball handling skills and excellent team work made them stand out and it was clear that this was the team to beat.
question_en: Based on the passage, what would most likely have happened if the mid-morning drizzle had persisted throughout the day?
mc_answer1_en: Zambia would have won against South Africa despite being the underdog
mc_answer2_en: The tournament organizers would have postponed the opening matches indefinitely
mc_answer3_en: South Africa's ball handling skills would have improved due to the wet conditions
mc_answer4_en: South Africa's disciplined defense would have been less effective due to slippery conditions

flores_passage_en: The temple of Artemis at Ephesus was destroyed on July 21, 356 BCE in an act of arson committed by Herostratus. According to the story, his motivation was fame at any cost. The Ephesians, outraged, announced that Herostratus' name never be recorded. The Greek historian Strabo later noted the name, which is how we know today. The temple was destroyed on the same night that Alexander the Great was born. Alexander, as king, offered to pay to rebuild the temple, but his offer was denied. Later, after Alexander died, the temple was rebuilt in 323 BCE.
question_en: If the Ephesians had decided to record Herostratus' name immediately after the arson, what would be the most likely consequence regarding the historical record of the event?
mc_answer1_en: Alexander the Great would have refused to offer to rebuild the temple.
mc_answer2_en: Herostratus would have been honored for his act instead of being remembered for his infamy.
mc_answer3_en: His name would be better known today, and Strabo might not have been needed to preserve it.
mc_answer4_en: The temple would have been rebuilt immediately without waiting for Alexander's offer.

flores_passage_en: """Panama Papers"" is an umbrella term for roughly ten million documents from Panamanian law firm Mossack Fonseca, leaked to the press in spring 2016. The documents showed fourteen banks helped wealthy clients hide billions of US dollars of wealth to avoid taxes and other regulations. British newspaper The Guardian suggested Deutsche Bank controlled roughly a third of the 1200 shell companies used to accomplish this. There were protests worldwide, several criminal prosecutions, and the leaders of the governments of Iceland and Pakistan both resigned."
question_en: According to the passage, what would most likely have been different if the 'Panama Papers' had not been leaked to the press in spring 2016?
mc_answer1_en: Deutsche Bank would have controlled a smaller portion of the shell companies.
mc_answer2_en: The leaked documents would not have shown fourteen banks helping clients hide wealth.

flores_passage_en: Soon after the outbreak of hostilities, Britain initiated a naval blockade of Germany. The strategy proved effective, cutting off vital military and civilian supplies, although this blockade violated generally accepted international law codified by several international agreements of the past two centuries. Britain mined international waters to prevent any ships from entering entire sections of ocean, causing danger to even neutral ships. Since there was limited response to this tactic, Germany expected a similar response to its unrestricted submarine warfare.
question_en: If Britain had not initiated the naval blockade of Germany after the outbreak of hostilities, which of the following would most likely have been true regarding Germany's expectations about international law and naval tactics?
mc_answer1_en: Germany would have anticipated Britain would continue to adhere to international law despite the blockade.
mc_answer2_en: Germany would have likely avoided adopting unrestricted submarine warfare, fearing a similar blockade response from Britain.
mc_answer3_en: Germany would have likely adopted unrestricted submarine warfare regardless, as its strategy was independent of Britain's blockade.
mc_answer4_en: Germany would have expected Britain to respect neutral ships in international waters, leading to more cooperation.

flores_passage_en: The United States Geological Survey international earthquake map showed no earthquakes in Iceland in the week prior. The Icelandic Meteorological Office also reported no earthquake activity in the Hekla area in the past 48 hours. The significant earthquake activity resulting in the phase change had took place on March 10 on the northeast side of the volcano's summit caldera. Dark clouds unrelated to any volcanic activity were reported at the base of the mountain. The clouds presented the potential for confusion as to whether an actual eruption had taken place.
question_en: If the significant earthquake activity on March 10 had not occurred, which of the following would most likely have been true regarding the phase change and public perception of an eruption?
mc_answer1_en: The phase change would not have happened, and the dark clouds would not have caused confusion about an eruption.
mc_answer2_en: The dark clouds would have been immediately recognized as unrelated to volcanic activity, preventing any confusion.
mc_answer3_en: The phase change would have still occurred due to other factors, but the dark clouds would not have been reported.
mc_answer4_en: The US Geological Survey would have detected earthquakes in Iceland in the week prior, contradicting the map data.

flores_passage_en: Anyone planning a visit to a country that could be considered a war zone should get professional training. A search of the Internet for 'Hostile environment course' will probably provide the address of a local company. A course will normally cover all the issues discussed here in far greater detail, usually with practical experience. A course will normally be from 2-5 days and will involve role play, a lot of first aid and sometimes weapons training. Books and magazines dealing with wilderness survival are common, but publications dealing with war zones are few.
question_en: If a person had not attended a hostile environment course, which of the following outcomes would most likely have occurred based on the passage?
mc_answer1_en: They would have been better prepared for weapons training than someone who attended the course.
mc_answer2_en: They would have received more detailed information than a course provides.
mc_answer3_en: They would have lacked practical experience in first aid and role play related to war zones.

flores_passage_en: Asynchronous communication encourages time for reflection and reaction to others. It allows students the ability to work at their own pace and control the pace of instructional information. In addition, there are fewer time restrictions with the possibility of flexible working hours. (Bremer, 1998) The use of the Internet and the World Wide Web allows learners to have access to information at all times. Students can also submit questions to instructors at any time of day and expect reasonably quick responses, rather than waiting until the next face-to-face meeting.
question_en: Based on the passage, if asynchronous communication were not available to students, which of the following consequences would most likely occur?
mc_answer1_en: Students would be unable to access information at any time of day.
mc_answer2_en: Students would lose the ability to control the pace of instructional information.
mc_answer3_en: Students would be forced to wait until the next face-to-face meeting to submit questions to instructors.
mc_answer4_en: Instructors would no longer be able to provide reasonably quick responses to student inquiries.

flores_passage_en: Humans are by far the most talented species in reading the minds of others. That means we are able to successfully predict what other humans perceive, intend, believe, know or desire. Among these abilities, understanding the intention of others is crucial. It allows us to resolve possible ambiguities of physical actions. For example, if you were to see someone breaking a car window, you would probably assume he was trying to steal a stranger’s car. He would need to be judged differently if he had lost his car keys and it was his own car that he was trying to break into.
question_en: If the person breaking the car window had not lost their car keys and it was actually their own car, how would the passage suggest observers would interpret the action?
mc_answer1_en: They would assume the person was practicing self-defense against an intruder.
mc_answer2_en: They would assume the person was trying to retrieve keys from inside the car.
mc_answer3_en: They would assume the person was attempting to break the window for no reason.
mc_answer4_en: They would assume the person was trying to steal a stranger’s car.

flores_passage_en: With the battle for France over, Germany began to get ready to invade the island of Britain. Germany code-named the attack “Operation Sealion”. Most of the British Army's heavy weapons and supplies had been lost when it evacuated from Dunkirk, so the army was fairly weak. But the Royal Navy was still much stronger than the German Navy (“Kriegsmarine”) and could have destroyed any invasion fleet sent across the English Channel. However, very few Royal Navy ships were based near the likely invasion routes as the admirals were afraid they would be sunk by German air attack.
question_en: If the British Army had not lost most of its heavy weapons and supplies at Dunkirk, what would most likely have been the outcome of the planned German invasion of Britain?
mc_answer1_en: The Germans would have been forced to abandon the invasion plan entirely.
mc_answer2_en: The Royal Navy would have had no reason to avoid the invasion routes.
mc_answer3_en: The invasion would have been easily repelled due to stronger British ground defenses.
mc_answer4_en: The outcome of the invasion would have been more uncertain, but the Royal Navy's role would have remained decisive.

flores_passage_en: "The Cook Islands are an island country in free association with New Zealand, located in Polynesia, in the middle of the South Pacific Ocean. It is an archipelago with 15 islands spread out over 2.2 million km2 of ocean. With the same time zone as Hawaii, the islands are sometimes thought of as ""Hawaii down under"". Though smaller, it reminds some elderly visitors of Hawaii before statehood without all the large tourist hotels and other development. The Cook Islands do not have any cities but are composed of 15 different islands. The main ones are Rarotonga and Aitutaki."
question_en: If the Cook Islands had not developed any large tourist hotels, which of the following statements would most accurately reflect a likely consequence based on the passage's description of the islands' character?
mc_answer1_en: The islands would likely still retain a quiet, less developed atmosphere reminiscent of Hawaii before statehood.
mc_answer2_en: The islands would be unable to attract any visitors from New Zealand or Hawaii.
mc_answer3_en: The islands would have to increase their size to compete with larger tourist destinations.
mc_answer4_en: The islands would be forced to establish cities to accommodate tourists.

flores_passage_en: There are many theories to how Sanskrit came into existence. One of them is about an Aryan migration from the west into India who brought their language with them. Sanskrit is an ancient language and is comparable to the Latin language spoken in Europe. The earliest known book in the world was written in Sanskrit. After the compilation of Upanishads, Sanskrit just faded due to hierarchy. Sanskrit is a very complex and rich language, which has served to be the source for many modern Indian languages, just like Latin is the source for European languages like French and Spanish.
question_en: Based on the passage, if the Upanishads had not been compiled, which of the following would most likely have been the case regarding the development of Sanskrit?
mc_answer1_en: Sanskrit would have been replaced by Aryan languages immediately
mc_answer2_en: Sanskrit would have become the primary language of modern Europe
mc_answer3_en: Sanskrit would have been written in Latin instead of its original form
mc_answer4_en: Sanskrit would have continued to be widely used without fading

flores_passage_en: News spread in the Red Lake community today as funerals for Jeff Weise and three of the nine victims were held that another student was arrested in connection with the school shootings of March 21. Authorities said little officially beyond confirming today's arrest. However, a source with knowledge of the investigation told the Minneapolis Star-Tribune that it was Louis Jourdain, 16-year old son of Red Lake Tribal Chairman Floyd Jourdain. It is not known at this time what charges will be laid or what led authorities to the boy but juvenile proceedings have begun in federal court.
question_en: If the arrest of Louis Jourdain had not occurred, what would most likely have been the immediate consequence for the Red Lake community based on the passage?
mc_answer1_en: Louis Jourdain would have faced immediate charges in federal court.
mc_answer2_en: Funerals for Jeff Weise and three victims would have been delayed.

flores_passage_en: The balance of power was a system in which European nations sought to maintain the national sovereignty of all European states. The concept was that all European nations had to seek to prevent one nation from becoming powerful, and thus national governments often changed their alliances in order to maintain the balance. The War of Spanish Succession marked the first war whose central issue was the balance of power. This marked an important change, as European powers would no longer have the pretext of being religious wars. Thus, the Thirty Years' War would be the last war to be labeled a religious war.
question_en: According to the passage, if the War of Spanish Succession had not occurred, what would most likely have been the status of the Thirty Years' War in terms of its classification?
mc_answer1_en: It would have been classified as a religious war.
mc_answer2_en: It would have been classified as a conflict over the balance of power.
mc_answer3_en: It would have been classified as a war to prevent any nation from becoming powerful.
mc_answer4_en: It would have been classified as a war for national sovereignty.

flores_passage_en: During the Revolutionary War, the thirteen states first formed a weak central government—with the Congress being its only component—under the Articles of Confederation. Congress lacked any power to impose taxes, and, because there was no national executive or judiciary, it relied on state authorities, who were often uncooperative, to enforce all its acts. It also had no authority to override tax laws and tariffs between states. The Articles required unanimous consent from all the states before they could be amended and states took the central government so lightly that their representatives were often absent.
question_en: If the Articles of Confederation had been easily amendable, what would most likely have been a direct consequence of this change, based on the passage's description of the government's structural weaknesses?
mc_answer1_en: The central government could have adapted its rules to address enforcement issues and interstate conflicts more effectively.
mc_answer2_en: State representatives would have attended congressional sessions more consistently due to increased influence.
mc_answer3_en: A national executive branch would have been automatically established to enforce laws.
mc_answer4_en: The central government would have gained the power to impose taxes without state approval.

flores_passage_en: A triceratops' teeth would have been able to crush not only leaves but even very tough branches and roots. Some scientists think Triceratops ate cycads, which are a type of plant that was common in the Cretaceous. These plants look like a small palm tree with a crown of sharp, spiky leaves. A Triceratops could have used its strong beak to strip off the leaves before eating the trunk. Other scientists argue that these plants are very poisonous so it is unlikely that any dinosaur ate them, even though today the sloth and other animals like the parrot (a descendant of the dinosaurs) can eat poisonous leaves or fruit.
question_en: What would have been the most likely outcome for Triceratops if cycads had not been a common plant in the Cretaceous period?
mc_answer1_en: They would have relied more on their beaks to strip leaves from other tough plants, but their diet would have remained unchanged.
mc_answer2_en: They would have needed to adapt their feeding strategies to consume different plants that were available at the time.
mc_answer3_en: They would have been forced to eat only the leaves of cycads, even though the trunks were more nutritious.
mc_answer4_en: They would have avoided eating cycads entirely due to the risk of poisoning from other plants.

flores_passage_en: If traveling in a developing country for the first time – or in a new part of the world – don't underestimate the potential culture shock. Many a stable, capable traveler has been overcome by the newness of developing world travel, where many little cultural adjustments can add up quickly. Especially in your initial days, consider splurging on Western-style and -quality hotels, food, and services to help acclimatize. Do not sleep on a mattress or pad on the ground in areas where you do not know the local fauna. If you are going to camp out, bring a camp cot or hammock to keep you away from snakes, scorpions and such.
question_en: If a traveler had not splurged on Western-style hotels and food during their initial days in a developing country, what would most likely be the consequence according to the passage?
mc_answer1_en: They would have avoided culture shock entirely due to better budget management.

flores_passage_en: "Traveling to Walt Disney World represents a major pilgrimage for many American families. The ""typical"" visit involves flying into Orlando International Airport, busing to an on-site Disney hotel, spending about a week without leaving Disney property, and returning home. There are infinite variations possible, but this remains what most people mean when they talk of ""going to Disney World"". Many tickets sold online through auction websites such as eBay or Craigslist are partially used multi-day park-hopper tickets. While this is a very common activity, it is prohibited by Disney: the tickets are non-transferable."
question_en: If a family had purchased a partially used multi-day park-hopper ticket from an auction website like eBay, what would most likely have been the consequence according to the passage?

flores_passage_en: Submarines are ships designed to travel underwater, and remain there for an extended amount of time. Submarines were used in World War I and World War II. Back then they were very slow and had a very limited shooting range. In the beginning of the war they mostly travelled on top of the sea, but as radar began developing and becoming more accurate the submarines were forced to go under water to avoid being seen. German submarines were called U-Boats. The Germans were very good at navigating and operating their submarines. Because of their success with submarines, after the war Germans aren't trusted to have many of them.
question_en: If radar had not developed and become more accurate during World War II, what would most likely have been the case for submarines?
mc_answer1_en: Submarines would have been used less frequently in the war
mc_answer2_en: Germans would have been trusted to own many submarines
mc_answer3_en: Submarines would have been forced to operate exclusively underwater
mc_answer4_en: Submarines would have remained on the surface of the sea more often

flores_passage_en: While project based learning should make learning easier and more interesting, scaffolding goes a step beyond. Scaffolding is not a method of learning but rather an aid that provides support to individuals whom are undergoing a new learning experience such as using a new computer program or beginning a new project. Scaffolds can be both virtual and real, in other words, a teacher is a form of scaffold but so is the little paperclip man in Microsoft Office. Virtual Scaffolds are internalized in the software and are meant to question, prompt, and explain procedures that may have been to challenging for the student to handle alone.
question_en: According to the passage, if scaffolding were not used in a new learning experience, what would most likely be the outcome?
mc_answer1_en: The learning experience would become more interesting but less effective, as scaffolding makes learning difficult.
mc_answer2_en: Students might struggle with procedures that are too challenging to handle alone, as scaffolds provide necessary support.

flores_passage_en: The stretch between Point Marion and Fairmont presents the most challenging driving conditions on the Buffalo-Pittsburgh Highway, passing frequently through isolated backwoods terrain. If you're not used to driving on country roads, keep your wits about you: steep grades, narrow lanes, and sharp curves predominate. Posted speed limits are noticeably lower than in previous and subsequent sections — commonly 35-40 mph (56-64 km/h) — and strict obedience to them is even more important than otherwise. Curiously, though, mobile phone service is much stronger here than along many other stretches of the route, e.g. the Pennsylvania Wilds.
question_en: If the posted speed limits on the stretch between Point Marion and Fairmont had been higher, similar to other sections of the Buffalo-Pittsburgh Highway, what would most likely have been the consequence for drivers unfamiliar with country roads?
mc_answer1_en: The speed limits would have matched those in the Pennsylvania Wilds, making driving safer overall.
mc_answer2_en: Drivers would have faced reduced risk due to improved mobile phone service coverage in that area.
mc_answer3_en: The likelihood of accidents would have increased because of steep grades, narrow lanes, and sharp curves combined with higher speeds.
mc_answer4_en: Mobile phone service would have become weaker compared to the Pennsylvania Wilds.

flores_passage_en: "Let's start with an explanation about Italy's plans. Italy was mainly the ""little brother"" of Germany and Japan. It had a weaker army and a weaker navy, although they had just built four new ships right before the beginning of the war. Italy's main goals were African countries. To capture those countries, they would need to have a troop launching pad, so as troops could sail across the Mediterranean Sea and invade Africa. For that, they had to get rid of British bases and ships in Egypt. Besides those actions, Italy's battleships were not supposed to do anything else. Now for Japan. Japan was an island country, just like Britain."
question_en: According to the passage, if Italy had not built four new ships right before the beginning of the war, what would have been the most likely consequence for their African campaign plans?
mc_answer1_en: Italy would have focused its attention on capturing European countries instead of African nations.
mc_answer2_en: Italy would have been unable to sail across the Mediterranean Sea to launch troops.

flores_passage_en: The work done was mostly theoretical, but the program was written to simulate observations made of the Sagittarius galaxy. The effect the team was looking for would be caused by tidal forces between the galaxy's dark matter and the Milky Way's dark matter. Just like the moon exerts a pull on the earth, causing tides, so does the Milky Way exert a force on the Sagittarius galaxy. The scientists were able to conclude that the dark matter affect other dark matter in the same way regular matter does. This theory says that most dark matter around a galaxy is located around a galaxy in a kind of halo, and is made of lots of small particles.
question_en: If the Milky Way had not exerted a gravitational force on the Sagittarius galaxy, which of the following outcomes would most likely have been observed by the team?
mc_answer1_en: The simulated observations would have shown no tidal forces affecting the distribution of dark matter particles.
mc_answer2_en: The scientists would have concluded that dark matter particles only interact with regular matter.
mc_answer3_en: The dark matter halo around the Sagittarius galaxy would have been more compact and dense.
mc_answer4_en: The program would have been unable to simulate any observations of the Sagittarius galaxy.

flores_passage_en: The most common cause for accidents in winter is slippery roads, pavements (sidewalks) and especially steps. At a minimum, you need footwear with suitable soles. Summer shoes are usually very slippery on ice and snow, even some winter boots are deficient. The pattern should be deep enough, 5 mm (1/5 inch) or more, and the material soft enough in cold temperatures. Some boots have studs and there is studded add-on equipment for slippery conditions, suitable for most shoes and boots, for the heels or heels and sole. Heels should be low and wide. Sand, gravel or salt (calcium chloride) is often scattered on roads or paths to improve traction.
question_en: If a pedestrian had not worn footwear with suitable soles during a winter storm, which of the following outcomes is most likely based on the passage?
mc_answer1_en: The pedestrian would have walked more quickly to avoid the slippery conditions.
mc_answer2_en: The pedestrian would have been protected by the salt scattered on the roads.
mc_answer3_en: The pedestrian would have likely slipped on icy steps due to inadequate traction.
mc_answer4_en: The pedestrian would have experienced increased warmth due to the absence of studs.

flores_passage_en: A World's Fair (commonly called World Exposition, or simply Expo) is large international festival of arts and sciences. Participating countries present artistic and educational displays in national pavilions to showcase world issues or their country's culture and history. International Horticultural Expositions are specialised events which showcase floral displays, botanical gardens and anything else to do with plants. Although in theory they can take place annually (so long as they are in different countries), in practice they are not. These events normally last anywhere between three and six months, and are held on sites no smaller than 50 hectares.
question_en: Based on the passage, which of the following best describes a counterfactual consequence if International Horticultural Expositions were held annually in the same country instead of different countries?
mc_answer1_en: The requirement for sites to be no smaller than 50 hectares would likely be waived to accommodate repeated use.
mc_answer2_en: The duration of the exposition would automatically shorten to one month to reduce costs.
mc_answer3_en: Participating countries would be required to present only artistic displays rather than educational ones.
mc_answer4_en: The logistical strain on the host country's infrastructure and resources would likely increase significantly over time.
flores_passage: ଏକ ବିଶ୍ୱ ମେଳା (ସାଧାରଣତଃ ବିଶ୍ୱ ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନୀ, କିମ୍ବା କେବଳ ଏକ୍ସପୋ କୁହାଯାଏ) ହେଉଛି କଳା ଏବଂ ବିଜ୍ଞାନର ଏକ ବୃହତ ଆନ୍ତର୍ଜାତୀୟ ମହୋତ୍ସବ । ଅଂଶଗ୍ରହଣକାରୀ ଦେଶମାନେ ବିଶ୍ୱ ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗ କିମ୍ବା ସେମାନଙ୍କ ଦେଶର ସଂସ୍କୃତି ଏବଂ ଇତିହାସକୁ ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶିତ କରିବା ପାଇଁ ଜାତୀୟ ପାଭିଲିୟନରେ କଳାତ୍ମକ ଏବଂ ଶିକ୍ଷାଗତ ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନୀ ଉପସ୍ଥାପନ କରନ୍ତି । ଆନ୍ତର୍ଜାତୀୟ ଉଦ୍ୟାନ କୃଷି ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନୀ ହେଉଛି ସ୍ୱତନ୍ତ୍ର କାର୍ଯ୍ୟକ୍ରମ ଯାହା ଫୁଲ ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନୀ, ଉଦ୍ଭିଦ ଉଦ୍ୟାନ ଏବଂ ଉଦ୍ଭିଦ ସହିତ ଜଡିତ ଅନ୍ୟାନ୍ୟ ଜିନିଷ ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନ କରେ । ଯଦିଓ ସିଦ୍ଧାନ୍ତରେ ସେମାନେ ବାର୍ଷିକ ଆୟୋଜନ କରିପାରିବେ (ଯେପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ସେମାନେ ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଦେଶରେ ଅଛନ୍ତି), ବାସ୍ତବରେ ସେମାନେ ନୁହଁନ୍ତି । ଏହି ଇଭେଣ୍ଟଗୁଡିକ ସାଧାରଣତ ତିନିରୁ ଛଅ ମାସ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ରହିଥାଏ ଏବଂ ୫୦ ହେକ୍ଟରରୁ କମ୍ ସାଇଟରେ ଆୟୋଜିତ ହୁଏ ।
question: ଏହି ଅନୁଚ୍ଛେଦକୁ ଆଧାର କରି, ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ କେଉଁଟି ଏକ ବିପରୀତ ପରିଣାମକୁ ସର୍ବୋତ୍ତମ ଭାବରେ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା କରେ ଯଦି ଅନ୍ତର୍ଜାତୀୟ ଉଦ୍ୟାନ କୃଷି ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନୀ ପ୍ରତିବର୍ଷ ଭିନ୍ନ ଭିନ୍ନ ଦେଶରେ ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତେ ସମାନ ଦେଶରେ ଆୟୋଜିତ ହୁଏ?

flores_passage_en: The first cases of the disease this season were reported in late July. The disease is carried by pigs, which then migrates to humans through mosquitos. The outbreak has prompted the Indian government to undertake such measures as deployment of pig catchers in seriously affected areas, distributing thousands of mosquito curtains and spraying pesticides. Several million vials of encephalitis vaccine have also been promised by the government, which will help prepare health agencies for next year. Plans for vaccines to be delivered to the historically most affected areas this year were delayed due to lack of funds and low prioritisation relative to other diseases.
question_en: If the Indian government had not delayed the vaccine delivery plans due to lack of funds and low prioritisation, what would most likely have been the consequence for the historically most affected areas this year?
mc_answer1_en: They would have received the vaccine doses earlier than planned, but the outbreak would have worsened due to increased mosquito activity.
mc_answer2_en: They would have received the vaccine doses earlier than planned, but the health agencies would have been unable to prepare for next year.
mc_answer3_en: They would have received the vaccine doses earlier than planned, but the government would have had to cancel the pig catcher deployment.
mc_answer4_en: They would have received the vaccine doses earlier than planned, improving immediate protection against the outbreak.

question: ଯଦି ଭାରତ ସରକାର ପାଣ୍ଠିର ଅଭାବ ଏବଂ କମ୍ ପ୍ରାଥମିକତା କାରଣରୁ ଟିକା ଯୋଗାଣ ଯୋଜନାରେ ବିଳମ୍ବ କରିନଥାନ୍ତେ, ତେବେ ଚଳିତ ବର୍ଷ ଐତିହାସିକ ଭାବେ ସର୍ବାଧିକ ପ୍ରଭାବିତ ଅଞ୍ଚଳ ପାଇଁ କ'ଣ ପରିଣାମ ହୋଇଥାନ୍ତା?

flores_passage_en: Hong Kong Island gives the territory of Hong Kong its name and is the place that many tourists regard as the main focus. The parade of buildings that make the Hong Kong skyline has been likened to a glittering bar chart that is made apparent by the presence of the waters of Victoria Harbour. To get the best views of Hong Kong, leave the island and head for the Kowloon waterfront opposite. The great majority of Hong Kong Island's urban development is densely packed on reclaimed land along the northern shore. This is the place the British colonisers took as their own and so if you are looking for evidence of the territory's colonial past, this is a good place to start.
question_en: If the British colonizers had not chosen the northern shore of Hong Kong Island for their own use, which of the following outcomes would most likely have occurred based on the passage?
mc_answer1_en: Tourists would have focused on the Victoria Harbour waters rather than the skyline.
mc_answer2_en: The reclaimed land would not have been developed for urban use at all.
mc_answer3_en: The colonial past would still be evident in the Kowloon waterfront area instead.
mc_answer4_en: The dense urban development along the northern shore might have been located elsewhere.

question: ଯଦି ବ୍ରିଟିଶ ଉପନିବେଶବାଦୀମାନେ ହଂକଂ ଦ୍ୱୀପର ଉତ୍ତର ତଟକୁ ନିଜ ବ୍ୟବହାର ପାଇଁ ଚୟନ କରିନଥାନ୍ତେ, ତେବେ ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ କେଉଁଟି ସମ୍ଭବତଃ ଘଟିଥାନ୍ତା?

flores_passage_en: Muhammad was deeply interested in matters beyond this mundane life. He used to frequent a cave that became known as “Hira‘” on the Mountain of “Noor” (light) for contemplation. he cave itself, which survived the times, gives a very vivid image of Muhammad’s spiritual inclinations. Resting on the top of one of the mountains north of Mecca, the cave is completely isolated from the rest of the world. In fact, it is not easy to find at all even if one knew it existed. Once inside the cave, it is a total isolation. Nothing can be seen other than the clear, beautiful sky above and the many surrounding mountains. Very little of this world can be seen or heard from inside the cave.
question_en: If Muhammad had not frequently visited the cave of Hira‘ for contemplation, which of the following outcomes would most likely have been true based on the passage's description of his spiritual inclinations?
mc_answer1_en: The sky above the cave would have appeared less clear and beautiful to him.
mc_answer2_en: He would have moved to a different mountain to find a more accessible place for worship.
mc_answer3_en: The cave itself would have been destroyed or forgotten due to lack of spiritual significance.
mc_answer4_en: He would have remained as deeply engaged with the mundane aspects of daily life without seeking spiritual isolation.
